subject: Proposal: Graduated Capacity Commit + Optional Early-Exit Window — renewal discussion
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudscale.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudScale Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — looking at graduated commit options

Hi Naomi,

Our renewal is coming up in May and we wanted to explore a different structure this time rather than a single-year flat commit. We expect our usage to grow over the next 24 months as product X scales across more regions, and procurement is asking for a contract that:

- starts with a modest committed baseline in year 1,
- increases the committed capacity in year 2 and year 3 (a graduated/phase-in schedule), and
- includes an ability for us to true-up usage quarterly against committed amounts.

We also need a limited early-exit option in case regulatory or budget changes force us to pause the program in year 1. That would be an exception, not the default — ideally a window with a fixed fee rather than open negotiation.

Can Redwood put together a strawman for a 3-year graduated commit with quarterly true-ups and a defined early-exit window? Also please call out how pricing would change versus our current flat commit, and any impact to SLA or capacity priority (we may need guaranteed burst capacity in month 6 onward).

Thanks — looping in procurement for timing.

Elaine

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear ask. This is absolutely something we can support; below is a quick outline and we'll attach a formal proposal this week.

High-level strawman (3-year graduated commit):
- Year 1: 40 reserved vGPU-hours / day equivalent (baseline)
- Year 2: 65 reserved vGPU-hours / day equivalent
- Year 3: 95 reserved vGPU-hours / day equivalent
- Quarterly true-up: usage reconciled to committed spend on a 90-day cadence with invoices/credits applied in the following invoice cycle.
- Early-exit window: a single, 60-day window in month 10–12 of year 1; exit fee = 30% of remaining committed year-1 value (negotiable tier).
- Burst capacity: guaranteed burst pool (up to +25% of baseline) available with priority routing; pricing for burst is blended at a reduced overage rate versus on-demand.

Impact to pricing / SLA: the graduated commit reduces your blended $/vGPU-hour by ~12% across the three-year term versus renewing at current flat rates but requires the true-up discipline. SLA, uptime SLAs, and priority routing remain at enterprise level; we can preserve existing latency targets for burst-enabled routes.

Next steps:
1) I will share a formal proposal PDF + pricing workbook (attached).
2) Marissa, can you confirm discount bands for a 3-year graduated structure?
3) Sean / Rishi — can engineering confirm the burst pool guarantees and whether we need any changes to routing policy for the first 12 months?

I attached a pencil proposal (CS_Graduated_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a pricing workbook (CS_Renewal_Pricing_Sheet.xlsx).

Best,

Thanks Naomi — reviewed the numbers. A couple of notes from pricing/finance:

- The blended 12% reduction is achievable if CloudScale signs the full 3-year term with the proposed stepped commits. If they want a smaller early-exit charge (e.g., 15%), we would need to reduce the annualized discount by ~3–4 percentage points.
- For the early-exit window timing: we recommend placing it between months 9–11 (aligned to your fiscal close) rather than month 10–12 — gives both sides time to reconcile usage and final invoices.
- True-up cadence: finance prefers semi-annual reconciliations for accounting simplicity, but we can do quarterly true-ups operationally and then roll them into semi-annual invoicing if that helps procurement.

Marissa

Elaine / team — from an engineering/ops perspective the plan is doable with two caveats:

1) Burst pool sizing: to guarantee the +25% burst without impacting other customers we recommend pre-reserving that capacity in the Dedicated pool starting month 6. That implies a small up-front allocation cost (one-time) to reserve the slot.
2) Gradual scaling automation: we'll add a scheduled scaling policy to automatically increase the reserved capacity at the year-2 and year-3 anniversaries. That requires a short config change and an ops redline in the SLA addendum.

I'll prepare a short technical addendum that outlines the reservation mechanics and the policy change — Naomi, I'll send that by EOD Friday.

—Sean
